problems.title: URL shortener
problems.prompt: Design a service that turns long URLs into short links and redirects visitors who open a short link. Links may be custom or expire. Expect heavy read traffic and a need for durability over years.

functional: Create a short URL for a long URL
Redirect a short URL to the original

tasks: Write rate: 100e6/(30*86400) = 38.6 per second on average
Storage over 5 years = 3.0 TB before replication
Number of characters in a base-62 code to hold 6e9 links: 6 (62^6 = 5.7e10)

rubric.point: States functional and non-functional requirements and scope
rubric.why: Shows that the design is driven by needs, not habit

rubric.point: Estimates read/write QPS and storage
rubric.why: Establishes that reads dominate and storage is modest

rubric.point: Defines API: create(longUrl, alias, ttl) and GET /{code}
Chooses a unique code strategy (counter or id ranges in base 62, or hash plus collision check)
rubric.why: Core deep-dive area for this problem

rubric.point: Explains key-value or simple relational store keyed by code
rubric.why: Access pattern is point lookup by key

rubric.point: Adds cache for hot links and a CDN or edge where useful
rubric.why: Reads dominate; caching gives large gains

rubric.point: Discusses redirect status choice (301 vs 302) and analytics impact
rubric.why: Shows understanding of browser caching effects

rubric.point: Handles expiry and cleanup
Addresses scaling: stateless app tier, replicated store, sharding by code
Mentions abuse prevention: rate limits, malware checks

referenceOutline.notes: Scope, custom aliases, expiry, analytics, scale
Row: code, longUrl, createdAt, expiresAt, ownerId
Clients, load balancer, stateless API servers, cache, key-value store, id allocator
Unique id allocation without a single bottleneck; cache sizing
Replication, cache stampede control, hot link handling

tradeoffs: Counter plus base-62 versus hashing: predictability and collisions versus simplicity
301 versus 302: fewer hits versus analytics control
Strong versus eventual consistency for newly created links
followUps: How do you prevent guessable codes?
How do you support analytics at scale without slowing redirects?
How would you handle a viral link?

rubric.why: Needed to route a message to the right connection

rubric.point: Uses a durable store with per-conversation ordering (sequence numbers)
rubric.why: Messages must not be lost or reordered

rubric.point: Handles offline users with storage plus push notification
Models delivery and read receipts as acknowledgements
Separates media upload to object storage with CDN, sending only references in chat
rubric.why: Large blobs do not belong in the message path

rubric.point: Explains group fan-out and limits on group size
Presence service with heartbeats and expiry
Partitions data by conversation id
rubric.why: Keeps ordered messages on one shard

rubric.point: Discusses end-to-end encryption and its impact on server features

Ordering, delivery guarantees, offline sync, group fan-out

tradeoffs: At-least-once delivery with dedupe versus at-most-once
Fan-out on write versus on read for large groups
